items.title: Access OpenAI gpt-oss Models at OCI Generative AI
items.content: OCI Generative AI currently supports pre-trained models of OpenAI gpt-oss, designed for both reasoning and agent tasks. `openai.gpt-oss-120b` is recommended for workloads complex and high demand resources and `openai.gpt-oss-20b` for local use that require lower latency. The models are available under demand and as endpoints that are deployed in dedicated AI clusters. The details of the functions are contained in Generative AI's documentation.

cover.alt: Access OpenAI gpt-oss Models at OCI Generative AI

items.title: Add Storage Files to Generative AI Applications
items.content:
The applications housed at OCI Generative AI support storage from persistent archives to preserve model artifacts, intermediate results, checkpoints and state from the application on a container path set up, even between restarts and redeployments.

When creating a housed application, they can be added up to 50 GB from storage files using the Console or API. This version supports the storage file with a single replica. The minimum and maximum number of replicas are set up in 1.

For more information, check Persistent File Storage for Hosted Applications. To start with, check Creating an Application.

cover.alt: Add Storage Files to Generative AI Applications

items.title: Create Generative AI Applications for Public Content
items.content:
By creating an application housed with OCI Generative AI, you can select `No authentication` to serve public content or run applications that manage their own authentication. Any person with endpoint access can send requests without authentication run by the platform.

To restrict access, implement authentication and authorization within the application. permissions OCI IAM remains necessary to manage and gain access from the application to other OCI services.

Query Authentication for details about authentication and Creating an Application for configuration steps.

cover.alt: Create Generative AI Applications for Public Content

items.title: Overall Availability of Generative AI
items.content:
OCI Generative AI now allows access to models at demand using routing profiles at 30 commercial regions OC1.

The routing profiles make it possible to call, from the playground of the user's region or using `Chat API`, `OCI Chat Completions API` or `OCI Responses API`, models that are supported and processed in other regions. The available API depends that the select model will admit it.

These regions also accept select Enterprise AI Agents and Enterprise AI Governance functions, including deployments housed, projects and API keys. To consult the regions and the authorized functions, see Regions with Non Local Model Processing. To start with, see Creating a Routing Profile.

items.title: Import Alibaba Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 into OCI Generative AI
items.content:
OCI Generative AI allows to import `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` model, create endpoints for it and use it to understand images and text. His capacity is set as `IMAGE_TEXT_TO_TEXT`.

The minimum form units of the dedicated AI cluster for this model are `A100_40G_X2`, `A100_80G_X1`, `H100_X1` and `H200_X1`.

The complete list of important models is in Models for Import. hardware availability by region at Hardware Unit Shapes by Region and the steps of deployment, at Managing Imported Models.

cover.alt: Import Alibaba Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 into OCI Generative AI

items.title: Import Alibaba Qwen3.8-Flash-Next to OCI Generative AI

The complete list of important models is in Models for Import. hardware availability by region at Hardware Unit Shapes by Region and the steps of deployment, at Managing Imported Models.

items.title: Import NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4 into OCI Generative AI
items.content:
The `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4` model can be imported to OCI Generative AI, where endpoints can be created and used to understand images and text.

Configure model capacity as `IMAGE_TEXT_TO_TEXT`. The minimum forms of dedicated AI cluster unit for this model are `H100_X2` and `H200_X2`.

See Models for Import to see complete list of important models, Hardware Unit Shapes by Region to get to know the availability of hardware by region and Managing Imported Models for deployment steps.

items.title: Using Sandboxes at OCI Generative AI
items.content:
Sandboxes is currently available at OCI Generative AI. Each sandbox is a temporary and managed Linux work space where developers and agents of AI can run shell code and commands. It has its own file system, network name space and process space.

With OCI CLI or SDK sandboxes can be created within a Generative AI project, select resources from Compute, define its duration and configure the command waiting times. They can also run commands, transmit their output and cancel them. Loading input files, downloading results and saving file system snapshots to create new sandboxes from saved files. as well as expand, stop and remove sandboxes.

The console allows you to enable sandboxes for a project, set up the network, check the details of each sandbox and monitor the use of resources and command performance. The general description is at Sandboxes in OCI Generative AI and the steps to start with, at Creating and Using a Sandbox.

cover.alt: Using Sandboxes at OCI Generative AI
